questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 10 days. On examination, it has indurated, clean-cut edges and a clean base. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged, firm, non-tender and rubbery. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Primary syphilis presents as a painless, indurated (hard) chancre with clean edges. The inguinal lymphadenopathy is non-tender and rubbery. Chancroid causes a painful ulcer with soft edges; herpes causes multiple painful vesicles/ulcers; LGV causes groove sign lymphadenopathy.

questions.q: A patient with leprosy presents with sudden onset facial palsy, loss of eyebrows (madarosis), and nasal stuffiness. Slit-skin smear shows a Bacterial Index (BI) of 4+. Which type of leprosy does this patient most likely have?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) is characterised by high bacterial load (BI 4-6+), madarosis (loss of eyebrows/eyelashes), nasal involvement, and diffuse infiltration of the face ('leonine facies'). Nerve involvement is late and symmetrical.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with a tense blister on normal-looking skin. Nikolsky sign is negative. Biopsy shows subepidermal blister with eosinophils. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense blisters on normal/erythematous skin, negative Nikolsky sign, subepidermal blistering with eosinophils, and linear IgG+C3 at BMZ on DIF. Target antigen is BPAG1 (BP230) and BPAG2 (BP180/collagen XVII).

questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer presents with a painless verrucous plaque on the foot with black dots on the surface and cauliflower-like appearance. KOH mount shows 'copper penny' (sclerotic) cells. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is caused by dematiaceous (black) fungi, most commonly Fonsecaea pedrosoi. Hallmark is 'copper penny' or 'Medlar bodies' (sclerotic cells) on KOH/histology. Lesions are warty/verrucous plaques. Sporotrichosis causes lymphocutaneous nodules; mycetoma has grains.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the lips recurring for 2 years. He reports burning and tingling 1 day before the eruption. Which antiviral drug, when taken during the prodrome, most effectively reduces the duration and severity of recurrences?
opts: Acyclovir 400mg three times daily for 5 days
questions.exp: Famciclovir 1500mg as a single dose (single-day therapy) is highly effective for episodic treatment of recurrent herpes labialis when initiated during the prodrome. It significantly reduces lesion healing time and viral shedding. Single-dose regimens improve adherence.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man on long-term methotrexate for psoriasis develops elevated LFTs and a liver biopsy shows periportal fibrosis. According to Roenigk classification, this corresponds to which grade?
questions.exp: Roenigk classification for methotrexate hepatotoxicity: Grade I = normal/fatty change; Grade II = portal inflammation; Grade IIIA = mild fibrosis (periportal); Grade IIIB = moderate to severe fibrosis; Grade IV = cirrhosis. Grade IIIA is periportal fibrosis.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with a well-demarcated, scaly plaque over the elbow with silvery scales. On scraping the scales, pinpoint bleeding points are seen. This sign is known as:
questions.exp: Auspitz sign (pin-point bleeding on removal of scales) is pathognomonic of psoriasis. It occurs because thin suprapapillary plates overlie dilated dermal capillaries; removal of scales strips the epidermis above these capillaries, causing bleeding.

questions.q: A child presents with honey-coloured crusted lesions around the mouth and nose. Gram stain of the exudate shows gram-positive cocci in chains. Which is the most appropriate topical antibiotic for localised impetigo?
questions.exp: Impetigo is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Group A Streptococcus. For localised non-bullous impetigo, topical mupirocin (pseudomonic acid) is first-line treatment. It is effective against both pathogens and achieves high tissue concentrations.

questions.q: A 40-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 count 80 cells/μL) presents with painful, necrotic ulcers on the perianal region. PCR confirms HSV-2. What is the most appropriate treatment regimen?
opts: Acyclovir 200mg five times daily for 5 days
Acyclovir 400mg three times daily for 5 days
Acyclovir 400mg five times daily for 7-10 days or until healed
questions.exp: In immunocompromised patients (HIV, CD4 <200), HSV episodes can be severe/chronic and require higher dose and longer duration. Standard regimen is acyclovir 400mg 5 times daily (or valacyclovir 1g BD) for 7-14 days or until clinical resolution. Chronic suppression may follow.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk, thickened greater auricular nerve, and claw hand. Slit-skin smear is negative. Biopsy shows epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells in the dermis infiltrating nerves. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Borderline tuberculoid (BT) leprosy with nerve involvement (claw hand = ulnar nerve) is classified as MB leprosy when >5 patches or nerve involvement is present. WHO-MDT for MB (rifampicin + dapsone + clofazimine) for 12 months is indicated. Claw hand indicates significant nerve damage.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with a butterfly rash over the face, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA is positive (1:640), anti-dsDNA is elevated, and complement C3/C4 are low. Which criterion is used for scoring SLE diagnosis in current guidelines?
questions.exp: The 2019 EULAR/ACR criteria replaced older criteria for SLE classification. It requires positive ANA as entry criterion, then allocates weighted scores across 7 clinical and 3 immunological domains. A score ≥10 classifies SLE. It has better sensitivity (96.1%) and specificity (93.4%) than older criteria.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with progressive tightening of the skin over the fingers causing inability to make a fist, telangiectasias, and dysphagia. Investigations reveal anti-centromere antibody positivity. What subset of systemic sclerosis does this represent?
questions.exp: Limited cutaneous SSc (formerly CREST: Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) is associated with anti-centromere antibodies. Skin involvement is limited to distal extremities and face. Anti-Scl-70 (topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse SSc.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male presents with a slow-growing pearly nodule with rolled edges and surface telangiectasias on the nose. Dermoscopy shows arborising vessels and blue-grey ovoid nests. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer. The nodular type classically presents as a pearly papule/nodule with rolled edges, telangiectasias, and central ulceration ('rodent ulcer'). Dermoscopy shows arborising vessels and blue-grey ovoid nests. Arises from basal layer of epidermis.

questions.q: A patient with genital warts (condylomata acuminata) is treated with podophyllin. Which of the following is a true statement about podophyllin?
opts: It is safe to use in pregnancy
It acts by inhibiting microtubule assembly
It can be self-applied by the patient
Maximum area that can be treated at one time is 10 cm²
questions.exp: Podophyllin is a plant-derived cytotoxic agent that acts as a mitotic poison by binding tubulin and inhibiting microtubule assembly (anti-mitotic). It is teratogenic and contraindicated in pregnancy. It must be applied by a clinician (not for self-application — podofilox/podophyllotoxin is for self-use). Max area per application is 10cm² (some guidelines say ≤0.5mL per visit).

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman has widespread erythema, skin peeling affecting >30% BSA following sulfonamide therapy. She has erosions of mouth and eyes. What is the most important initial management step?
opts: Immediate withdrawal of the offending drug and transfer to burns unit
questions.exp: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN; >30% BSA detachment) is a dermatological emergency. The FIRST and most critical step is immediate withdrawal of the causative drug. Transfer to a burns unit/ICU for supportive care (fluid/electrolyte balance, wound care, prevention of infection) is essential. Drug withdrawal alone can halt progression. IVIG/cyclosporine are adjuncts but not the first step.

questions.q: A 20-year-old man presents with multiple target lesions on the palms and soles following a cold sore 10 days ago. There are no mucosal lesions. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Erythema multiforme (EM) minor presents with target (iris) lesions on acral sites (palms/soles), typically triggered by HSV-1/2 infection. It lacks significant mucosal involvement (<1 site). SJS involves mucosae and >10% BSA detachment. The post-herpes timing is classic for EM.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with diffuse scaling of the scalp with broken-off hair stubs at the follicular orifice. KOH shows arthroconidia inside the hair shaft. Wood's lamp examination shows no fluorescence. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Endothrix tinea capitis (arthroconidia inside hair shaft) is caused by Trichophyton species (T. tonsurans, T. violaceum, T. soudanense). Endothrix infections do NOT fluoresce under Wood's lamp. Ectothrix infections (Microsporum species) show green fluorescence. T. violaceum is common in India.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with violaceous papules on the flexor aspect of the wrists, Wickham's striae on oral mucosa, and intense pruritus. What is the characteristic histopathological finding in lichen planus?
opts: Saw-tooth rete ridges with a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate hugging the dermo-epidermal junction
Dermal neutrophilic infiltrate with nuclear dust
questions.exp: Lichen planus histology shows: hyperkeratosis, wedge-shaped hypergranulosis, irregular acanthosis with saw-tooth rete ridges, vacuolar degeneration of basal layer, and a band-like (lichenoid) lymphocytic infiltrate at the DEJ. Colloid (Civatte) bodies representing apoptotic keratinocytes are also seen.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with a persistent violaceous plaque on the lower leg with a central adherent yellowish scale. Histology shows transepidermal elimination of collagen fibres through follicular infundibula. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Kyrle disease (hyperkeratosis follicularis et parafollicularis in cutem penetrans) shows transepidermal elimination of cellular debris/collagen through dilated follicles and eccrine ducts. It is associated with diabetes and renal failure. Reactive perforating collagenosis follows skin trauma; EPS eliminates elastic fibres.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman undergoing PUVA therapy for psoriasis asks about contraindications. Which of the following is an absolute contraindication to PUVA therapy?
opts: History of non-melanoma skin cancer 5 years ago
questions.exp: Pregnancy is an absolute contraindication to PUVA (psoralen + UVA) therapy because psoralens are mutagenic and teratogenic. Other absolute contraindications include lupus erythematosus, xeroderma pigmentosum, and cataract. History of SCC is a relative contraindication (absolute for melanoma). Skin type I requires dose adjustment, not absolute contraindication.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with a painless, firm, nodular swelling on the dorsal foot that has been slowly growing for 6 months. Aspiration yields characteristic sulfur granules. Gram stain of granules shows gram-positive branching filaments. What is the treatment of choice?
opts: Penicillin G IV followed by oral amoxicillin for 6-12 months
questions.exp: Actinomycetoma caused by Actinomyces (gram-positive anaerobic bacteria) is treated with high-dose penicillin G IV (10-20 MU/day) for 4-6 weeks followed by oral amoxicillin/amoxiclav for 6-12 months. Sulfur granules are pathognomonic. Eumycetoma (fungal) is treated with itraconazole ± surgical excision.

questions.q: A 25-year-old pregnant woman (28 weeks) presents with intensely pruritic, urticarial papules and plaques in the periumbilical area sparing the umbilicus itself and spreading to thighs and buttocks. Investigations are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy (PEP/PUPPP) typically begins in the third trimester within striae on the abdomen, classically SPARING the umbilicus. It is more common in primigravidas and with multiple gestations. DIF is negative. Pemphigoid gestationis involves the periumbilical area but DIF shows C3 at BMZ.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a pigmented lesion on the sole with irregular borders, variegated colour (tan, brown, black areas), and diameter of 12mm. ABCDE criteria are concerning. Dermoscopy shows a parallel ridge pattern. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Acral lentiginous melanoma (ALM) most commonly presents on palms, soles, and nail apparatus. On dermoscopy, ALM shows parallel ridge pattern (pigment along dermatoglyphic ridges), while benign acral nevi show parallel furrow pattern (pigment in furrows). ALM is the most common melanoma in Asians and darker skin types.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with palpable purpura on the lower limbs, arthralgia, and haematuria. Biopsy of skin lesion shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA deposits on immunofluorescence. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: IgA vasculitis (formerly Henoch-Schönlein purpura) is characterised by IgA deposition in small vessel walls. Classic tetrad: palpable purpura (lower limbs/buttocks), arthralgia, abdominal pain, and renal involvement (haematuria/proteinuria). DIF showing IgA deposits in dermal vessels is diagnostic.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a non-scarring, diffuse hair loss with widening of the central part. Pull test is positive. Trichoscopy shows yellow dots, black dots, and broken hairs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Alopecia areata on trichoscopy shows: yellow dots (dystrophic follicles with sebaceous secretion), black dots (broken hairs at scalp level = cadaverised hairs), broken hairs, exclamation mark hairs, and micro-exclamation mark hairs. Positive pull test indicates active disease. Androgenetic alopecia shows peripilar signs and miniaturisation.

questions.q: A 20-year-old woman presents with multiple hypopigmented macules on the trunk with fine branny scales. KOH preparation shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Tinea versicolor (Pityriasis versicolor) is caused by Malassezia furfur (now classified as M. globosa and other species). KOH preparation shows the classic 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance — short, curved hyphae (spaghetti) and yeast cells (meatballs). Wood's lamp shows golden-yellow fluorescence.

questions.q: A 65-year-old male farmer presents with a non-healing ulcer on the dorsum of hand for 4 months. He recalls a boil at the same site weeks earlier. Biopsy shows pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, microabscesses, and large yeast cells with broad-based buds. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: North American blastomycosis (Blastomyces dermatitidis) presents with warty/verrucous ulcerating plaques, often on exposed sites. Histology shows pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia (PEH), microabscesses, and large yeast cells (8-15μm) with thick walls and BROAD-BASED buds. Paracoccidioidomycosis shows 'steering wheel/pilot wheel' multi-budding pattern.

questions.q: A 19-year-old woman presents with hyperpigmentation over sun-exposed areas of the face with accentuation of the malar areas after starting oral contraceptive pills 6 months ago. What is the best treatment option?
opts: Triple combination cream (hydroquinone + tretinoin + topical steroid) with sun protection
questions.exp: Melasma (chloasma) treatment: the most effective topical treatment is the Modified Kligman's formula — triple combination of hydroquinone (bleaching agent), tretinoin (accelerates epidermal turnover), and mild topical corticosteroid (reduces irritation). Strict photoprotection is mandatory. Oral tranexamic acid is an adjunct. Monotherapy with HQ is less effective than the combination.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a recurrent, painful, indurated nodule on the occipital scalp and nape of neck with perifollicular pustules and sinus tracts. The area shows significant scarring alopecia. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dissecting cellulitis of the scalp (Hoffman's disease) presents with painful fluctuant boggy nodules and plaques, interconnecting sinus tracts, purulent discharge, and severe scarring alopecia predominantly on the vertex and occiput. It is part of the follicular occlusion tetrad. Folliculitis keloidalis nuchae is on the nape with keloidal papules/plaques.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man with extensive plaque psoriasis is started on a biologic targeting IL-17A. After 3 months, he develops oral candidiasis. Which biologic is he most likely receiving?
questions.exp: Secukinumab (anti-IL-17A) and ixekizumab are associated with an increased risk of mucocutaneous candidiasis. IL-17A plays a crucial role in host defence against Candida at mucosal surfaces. Adalimumab raises risk of opportunistic infections including TB. Ustekinumab and guselkumab have lower candidiasis risk.
